title: Talking about yesterday
title_target: きのう なにを しましたか — Kinō nani o shimashita ka
goal: Talk about what has already happened: the past tense of verbs, adjectives and nouns; chaining events with the て-form; and putting together a short, well-ordered story.
bekal: using ました and ませんでした
putting い- and な-adjectives in the past
linking events with ～てから and ～てください
telling about your weekend in five sentences

dialogs.title: 会話 1 — Last weekend
dialogs.intro: Tanaka and Ani swap stories on Monday morning. This is the last dialogue of the module — almost everything you learned in the previous nine units shows up here at once.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [アニさん|Ani-san]、[しゅうまつは|shūmatsu wa] [なにを|nani o] [しましたか|shimashita ka]。
lines.id: Ani, what did you do on the weekend?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [どようびに|Doyōbi ni] [ともだちと|tomodachi to] [きょうとへ|Kyōto e] [いきました|ikimashita]。
lines.id: On Saturday I went to Kyoto with a friend.
lines.literal: Saturday — on — friend — with — Kyoto — to — went.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [どうでしたか|Dō deshita ka]。
lines.id: How was it?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [とても|Totemo] [きれいでした|kirei deshita]。[おてらを|Otera o] [みて|mite]、[しゃしんを|shashin o] [たくさん|takusan] [とりました|torimashita]。
lines.id: It was beautiful. I saw temples and took lots of photos.
lines.literal: very — beautiful — was. temple — [object] — see-and, photo — [object] — many — took.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [ひとは|Hito wa] [おおかったですか|ōkatta desu ka]。
lines.id: Was it crowded?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [はい|Hai]、[すごく|sugoku] [おおかったです|ōkatta desu]。でも、[たのしかったです|tanoshikatta desu]。
lines.id: Yes, really crowded. But it was fun.
lines.literal: yes, terribly — many-were — is. but, fun-was — is.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [なにか|Nanika] [かいましたか|kaimashita ka]。
lines.id: Did you buy anything?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [おみやげを|Omiyage o] [かいました|kaimashita]。[でも|Demo]、[すこし|sukoshi] [たかかったです|takakatta desu]。
lines.id: I bought some souvenirs. But they were a bit pricey.
lines.literal: souvenir — [object] — bought. but, a-little — expensive-was — is.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [にちようびは|Nichiyōbi wa]？
lines.id: And Sunday?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [どこも|Doko mo] [いきませんでした|ikimasen deshita]。[つかれましたから|Tsukaremashita kara]、[うちで|uchi de] [やすみました|yasumimashita]。
lines.id: I didn't go anywhere. I was tired, so I rested at home.
lines.literal: where — even — didn't-go. got-tired — because, home — at — rested.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [それは|Sore wa] [よかったですね|yokatta desu ne]。
lines.id: Good for you.

notes: **どうでしたか = “how was it?”** — the past of どうですか. It's the standard opening question about a past experience, and you'll be asked it often.
**どこも + negative verb = “not anywhere”.** The pattern question word + も + negative gives “not … any”: なにも たべませんでした (didn't eat anything), だれも いませんでした (there was nobody).
**なにか = something.** Compare なにも, which always pairs with a negative. One kana different, and the sentence flips direction.
**よかったです has a warm second meaning:** besides “was good”, it also means “I'm glad”. それはよかったですね = “I'm glad to hear that”. One of the most common ways to respond to good news.
**つかれました = I'm tired**, just like おなかがすきました in Unit 7: a past form for a **present** state. Japanese sees it as “have become tired”.
**おみやげ = souvenirs**, and this is more than a habit: bringing back souvenirs for coworkers after a trip is a custom genuinely followed in Japanese offices.

grammars.title: The past tense — three kinds of words, three ways
body: This is the most important summary in the module. Note that **verbs** and **[い|i]-adjectives** change themselves, while **[な|na]-adjectives** and **nouns** change their [です|desu].

head: Type
Present
Past
Past negative
rows: [しずかじゃありませんでした|shizuka ja arimasen deshita]
[がくせいじゃありませんでした|gakusei ja arimasen deshita]

after: ⚠️ **Mistake number one:** writing **[たかいでした|takai deshita]**. An [い|i]-adjective puts **itself** in the past ([たかかった|takakatta]), not its [です|desu]. This mistake hangs on even among intermediate learners — nip it in the bud now.
**The quick way for [い|i]-adjectives:** drop [い|i], add **[かった|katta]**. [たかい|takai] → [たか|taka] + [かった|katta] → [たかかった|takakatta]. The negative: [たかくない|takakunai] → [たかくなかった|takaku nakatta].

grammars.title: Making the [て|te]-form
body: The **[て|te]-form** is a major hub of Japanese: it gives you requests (～[てください|te kudasai]), permission (～[てもいいですか|te mo ii desu ka]), ongoing states (～[ています|te imasu]) and linked events (～[て|te]、～).
How you form it from the [ます|masu] form depends on the last sound before [ます|masu]:

head: ます ending
Becomes
Example
rows: [かいます|kaimasu] → [かって|katte] · [まちます|machimasu] → [まって|matte]
[のみます|nomimasu] → [のんで|nonde] · [よみます|yomimasu] → [よんで|yonde]
[かきます|kakimasu] → [かいて|kaite] · [ききます|kikimasu] → [きいて|kiite]
[たべます|tabemasu] → [たべて|tabete] · [みます|mimasu] → [みて|mite]
[します|shimasu] → [して|shite] · [きます|kimasu] → [きて|kite] · [いきます|ikimasu] → [いって|itte]

after: **Don't memorize this table all at once.** What works for nearly every learner: memorize the [て|te]-forms of the ten verbs you use most, as whole words. The pattern will emerge from experience, not from the table.
⚠️ **[いきます|ikimasu] → [いって|itte]** is the only exception in the ～[き|ki] group. The rest ([かきます|kakimasu] → [かいて|kaite]) follow the pattern.

dialogs.title: 会話 2 — Chaining events
dialogs.intro: Budi tells his teacher about his day. Notice how the て-form links events in sequence without repeating “and then” over and over.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [ブディさん|Budi-san]、[きのうは|kinō wa] [どうでしたか|dō deshita ka]。
lines.id: Budi, how was yesterday?

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [あさ|Asa] [おきて|okite]、[あさごはんを|asagohan o] [たべて|tabete]、[がっこうへ|gakkō e] [きました|kimashita]。
lines.id: In the morning I got up, had breakfast and came to school.
lines.literal: morning — get-up-and, breakfast — [object] — eat-and, school — to — came.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [ごごは|Gogo wa]？
lines.id: And the afternoon?

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [じゅぎょうが|Jugyō ga] [おわってから|owatte kara]、[としょかんで|toshokan de] [べんきょうしました|benkyō shimashita]。
lines.id: After class finished, I studied at the library.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [なんじまで|Nanji made] [べんきょうしましたか|benkyō shimashita ka]。
lines.id: Until what time did you study?

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: 8[じまでです|ji made desu]。[それから|Sorekara] [ともだちと|tomodachi to] [ばんごはんを|bangohan o] [たべました|tabemashita]。
lines.id: Until eight. After that I had dinner with friends.
lines.literal: 8 — o'clock — until — is. after-that — friend — with — dinner — [object] — ate.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [なにを|Nani o] [たべましたか|tabemashita ka]。
lines.id: What did you eat?

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [カレーを|Karē o] [たべました|tabemashita]。[やすくて|Yasukute] [おいしかったです|oishikatta desu]。
lines.id: Curry. It was cheap and tasty.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [しゅくだいは|Shukudai wa] [しましたか|shimashita ka]。
lines.id: Did you do your homework?

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [すみません|Sumimasen]、[まだです|mada desu]。[きょう|Kyō] [うちへ|uchi e] [かえってから|kaette kara] [します|shimasu]。
lines.id: Sorry, not yet. I'll do it today after I get home.
lines.literal: sorry, not-yet — is. today — home — to — return-after — do.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [わかりました|Wakarimashita]。[がんばってください|Ganbatte kudasai]。
lines.id: All right. Do your best.

notes: **～て、～て、～ました** — a sequence of events marks only the **last verb** as past. The earlier ones just take the て-form. This saves a lot, and instantly makes your story flow instead of sounding choppy.
**～てから = after ～.** Unlike plain ～て, てから stresses that the first action is fully finished first. かえってからします = I'll do it **after** I get home.
**まだです = not yet.** A short, polite answer to “have you…?”. The opposite: もうしました (already did).
**がんばってください = do your best / good luck.** One of the most typically Japanese phrases, used for anything: exams, work, matches. The casual version is がんばって; to encourage yourself, がんばります.
**しゅくだい = homework**, literally “lodging task”. The verb is します: しゅくだいをします.
**カレー** — Japanese curry differs from Indian or Thai curry: sweeter, thicker, served over rice. It's one of the most common home-cooked meals in Japan.

grammars.title: Chaining events with the [て|te]-form
body: Japanese doesn't link clauses with a word for “and”. It uses the [て|te]-form of the earlier verb instead. The order follows time — the first event comes first.

head: Form
Example
Meaning
rows: I got up, ate, then went.
I'll do it after I get home.
[すわっても|Suwatte mo] [いいですか|ii desu ka]。
[とうきょうに|Tōkyō ni] [すんでいます|sunde imasu]。

after: **One form, six uses.** That's why the [て|te]-form deserves practice until it comes out without thinking. If there's one thing from this module to carry to the next level, this is it.

grammars.title: Dates and months
body: To talk about the past, you need dates. Months are very regular — just number + **[がつ|gatsu]**. Days 1 to 10 are irregular and must be memorized; the rest are number + **[にち|nichi]**.
after: **The order goes from big to small:** 2026[ねん|nen] 8[がつ|gatsu] 21[にち|nichi] = August 21, 2026. Year first, then month, then day — the same way Japanese addresses are written.

**The rest are regular:** 11日 = [じゅういちにち|jūichinichi], 15日 = [じゅうごにち|jūgonichi], 30日 = [さんじゅうにち|sanjūnichi]. Only the ones marked in the table are irregular — learn the first ten and the rest take care of themselves.

blocks.text: The final A1 skill is telling something that has happened, in order. This five-sentence frame works for any story:

head: Part
Pattern
Example
rows: [どようびに|Doyōbi ni] [きょうとへ|Kyōto e] [いきました|ikimashita]。
[ともだちと|Tomodachi to] [いきました|ikimashita]。
[おてらを|Otera o] [みて|mite]、[しゃしんを|shashin o] [とりました|torimashita]。
[とても|Totemo] [たのしかったです|tanoshikatta desu]。

blocks.title: A complete example
items: [せんしゅうの|Senshū no] [にちようびに|nichiyōbi ni] [ともだちと|tomodachi to] [うみへ|umi e] [いきました|ikimashita]。
[でんしゃで|Densha de] 2[じかん|jikan] [ぐらい|gurai] [かかりました|kakarimashita]。
[うみで|Umi de] [およいで|oyoide]、[しゃしんを|shashin o] [たくさん|takusan] [とりました|torimashita]。
[てんきが|Tenki ga] [よくて|yokute]、[とても|totemo] [たのしかったです|tanoshikatta desu]。
[こんど|Kondo] [かぞくと|kazoku to] [また|mata] [いきたいです|ikitai desu]。

Last Sunday I went to the beach with a friend. It took about 2 hours by train. At the beach I swam and took lots of photos. The weather was nice and it was great fun. Next time I want to go again with my family.

blocks.text: Now write your own version, about your actual weekend. Five sentences. This is the module's last homework, and the most useful.

blocks.title: もう and まだ
items: **[もう|Mō] [しましたか|shimashita ka]。** — Have you done it yet?
**[はい|Hai]、[もう|mō] [しました|shimashita]。** — Yes, already.
**[いいえ|Iie]、[まだです|mada desu]。** — Not yet.
⚠️ Don't answer いいえ、しませんでした for “not yet” — that means “I didn't do it (and won't)”. まだです leaves the possibility open, which is usually what you mean.

[がんばります|ganbarimasu] 頑張ります

exercises.prompt: Translate into Japanese. Write in rōmaji.
items: Yesterday I went to Kyoto.
It was great fun.
I didn't eat anything.
I'll do my homework after I get home.
Next time I want to go again.

answers: たべました — いきました — たかかったです — でした — でした — よかったです
いきませんでした — たべませんでした — しませんでした — きませんでした — のみませんでした
たべて — のんで — かいて — して — きて — いって
きのう ともだち と きょうと へ いきました — とても たのしかった です — おきて あさごはん を たべて がっこう へ いきました — うち へ かえって から しゅくだい を します — どこ も いきません でした — つかれました から うち で やすみました
What did you do on the weekend? — Kyoto was very beautiful. — There were so many people. — On Sunday I didn't go anywhere. — After class finished, I studied at the library.
kinō Kyōto e ikimashita — totemo tanoshikatta desu — nanimo tabemasen deshita — kaette kara shukudai o shimasu — kondo mata ikitai desu
wave: This is the last unit, so the review covers everything: read **the first dialogue of every unit** aloud, one a day for ten days, without looking at the translation. Whatever no longer needs the rōmaji above it is truly yours — and there's usually a surprising amount of it.
